title: Sessions
summary: A Session is one conversation with Claude Code. worfy runs your Sessions itself, each as a Node on the Canvas, and the Orchestrator is the Project's main Session. Sessions you started in a terminal or Claude desktop show up too, read-only.

scene.description: Sessions in worfy. On the Canvas lie the Orchestrator, the Project's main Session; a Session, which starts a Subagent shown to its right; and a read-only Session. worfy passes your messages from the Orchestrator and the Session to Claude Code. Claude Code writes each conversation to a file in Claude home and reports the Limits. worfy reads the file, adds the live events and shows both as the Transcript. A terminal or Claude desktop writes its Sessions there too; worfy shows such a Session as a read-only Node, and Resume continues it in worfy once it has finished.

labels.step1: You write to a Session from its Node or from the Session view, and worfy passes the message to Claude Code. A message sent during a turn waits in a queue.
labels.step2: Claude Code writes the conversation to a file in Claude home. worfy reads the file, adds the live events and shows both as the Transcript.
labels.step3: A Session can start Subagents. Each one gets a Node to the right of its Session, with its status.
labels.step4: Sessions started in a terminal or Claude desktop show up as read-only Nodes. Resume continues one in worfy once it has finished.
labels.step5: Claude Code reports the Limits: how much of your subscription's 5-hour and 7-day windows is used.

flow.description: The data flow of a Session. In the renderer: the Limits bars, the renderer store, the Session view and the Subagent tree. In the main process: the LimitsTracker, the Session, the transcript reader and the SubagentReader. On the side of Claude Code: its process and Claude home. The Session view sends a message on agent.send to the Session, which puts it in the input queue of the Claude Code process. The process answers with SDK messages; the Session sends them as AgentEvents on agent.event to the renderer store, which passes the live events to the Session view. Each rate_limit_event goes from the Session to the LimitsTracker, which sends limits.changed to the Limits bars. The process writes the transcript into Claude home; the transcript reader reads its new lines and answers claudeHome.transcript to the Session view. The SubagentReader reads what was appended to the Subagents' files and answers claudeHome.subagents to the Subagent tree.

text: Each Session is one long-running query of the Claude Agent SDK in the main process. Its input is a queue, so a new message goes into the running Claude Code process instead of starting another one. Each SDK message becomes AgentEvents, which go to every window on agent.event.

The transcript file is the record, and the renderer store saves nothing. Transcript lines are parsed into the same AgentEvents as the live ones, so one fold draws both. worfy only reads the transcripts in Claude home.
The Limits merge three sources: each Session's rate_limit_event, the rate_limits that Claude Code gives the status line, and a usage request.

limits: A message takes up to 20 attachments. An image may be up to 3.75 MB, and a file copied into the Project's data folder up to 20 MB.
A Transcript opens on the last 4 MB of its file, and Load earlier reads further back. The renderer keeps the newest 5000 live events of each Session.
Only a finished Session can be resumed, because two processes must not write one transcript.
